title: Universal components check
description: Settings of the universal components check run by `lint:structure` (components.js). The check reads each package's `package.json#exports`, resolves every entry the way the app bundlers do, follows re-exports to the declaring module and collects the public components per entry and per platform. R1: a universal component is exported on both platforms under the same name. R2: both implementations of a universal component take one props type, declared in one unsuffixed module, the contract. R3: the contract is neutral: no platform import, type, prop or gesture name. R4: a platform module that declares a universal component exports components only. R5: a component is exported from universal entries or from platform entries, never both. Waivers live in exceptions.js, not here. See docs/adr/universal-components.md.

$schema.description: Path to this schema, for editor validation and completion.

ignoredEntryPrefixes.description: Test support entries the check skips. An `exports` subpath is skipped when one of its `/`-separated segments starts with one of these prefixes: with `test`, `./testing` and `./testing/module-mock` are skipped. Matching is case-sensitive. Keep the list short: a skipped entry can ship components no rule sees.

platformEntries.description: Subpaths that are platform entries when their target is a plain string, mapped to their platform. A platform entry is resolved once, for its platform, and must point at a module of its own that carries its platform's suffix (`.web.*`, or `.native.*`, `.ios.*`, `.android.*`). The same subpath with a `react-native` condition is a universal entry instead.

conditions.description: Export conditions each platform tries, in order, to pick an entry's file. The first key of the entry's condition object that appears in the list wins, as in Node's resolution. An entry whose condition object has `react-native` is a universal entry.

extensions.description: Extensions tried, in order, to resolve a relative import without an extension: first `<path><ext>`, then `<path>/index<ext>`. An import with its own suffix (`./A.native`) also tries the exact file first. Each list must mirror its bundler, or the check reports what the app does not ship.

web.description: Desktop order, from `resolve.extensions` in apps/ledger-live-desktop/tools/rspack/rspack.renderer.ts: `.web` files first, then unsuffixed ones.

native.description: Mobile order, from `Repack.getResolveOptions(platform, { preferNativePlatform: true })`. Re.Pack ranks the extension before the suffix: for each of `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx` it tries `.ios`, `.android`, `.native`, then no suffix, so `A.ts` wins over `A.native.tsx`. iOS and Android share one list: a package does not ship different components to each.

componentWrappers.description: Calls whose result is still a component, such as `memo(...)` or `React.memo(...)`. A PascalCase named export of a `.tsx` module is a component when it is a function declaration, a function or arrow expression, or a call to one of these, called directly or as a property (`React.forwardRef`). `createContext` results are not components, so leave it out.

bannedImportPrefixes.description: R3. Module specifiers a contract may not import or re-export from, matched as prefixes: `react-native` also covers `react-native-svg`. An `import("...")` type counts too. A contract holds the props of both platforms, so it cannot depend on one platform's packages.

neutralReactTypes.description: R3. The types a contract may reference from `react`, whether imported, read as `React.X` or as `import("react").X`. React also exports the DOM types of react-dom (`ChangeEvent`, `CSSProperties`, `HTMLAttributes`), so the list names the neutral ones and rejects the rest. A global type the ECMAScript library of the installed TypeScript does not declare, such as `Element` or `MouseEvent`, is rejected without a list, and React Native types need an import that `bannedImportPrefixes` rejects. The check reads names, not types: an alias declared in another module escapes it.

bannedPropNames.description: R3. Props a contract may not declare, matched exactly. Each implementation styles its own surface.

gestureWords.description: R3. Words a callback prop may not contain, matched on whole camelCase words: `Press` rejects `onPress` and `onEditPress`, not `onPressureChange`. A callback prop is one named `on` plus an uppercase letter, a method or a property with a function type. Callbacks name the user's intent instead, such as `onEdit`.

bannedCallbackNames.description: R3. DOM event names a callback prop may not take, matched on the whole name. `*` stands for zero or more camelCase words: `onKey*` matches `onKeyDown`, not `onKeyboardShow`.
